# service: hub: runtime for the pages at maintainer.localhost

## Motivation

The local service ([[MAIN-151]]) answers one static page. The v0.3 line ([[MAIN-M2]]) turns it into a hub: `/status`, `/inbox` and `/tablo` over what maintainer already works with, the local checkouts and their issue mirrors in `.github/issues` and `.github/roadmap`. The three pages share one runtime: configuration, an index of the mirrors, the task model and its queries, a cached status snapshot, a JSON API, the HTTP security that private data needs, and a frontend shell with the shared components. The runtime comes first and owns every resource handler and contract; the pages ([[MAIN-156]], [[MAIN-157]], [[MAIN-158]]) add presentation only.

## Expected behavior

- **Frontend.** A Preact + TypeScript + Vite application under `web/`, inside the root Go module; `web/dist` is committed and embedded with `go:embed`, so `go install …` and GoReleaser build the binary without Node. The service serves the application document at `/status`, `/inbox` and `/tablo` only, redirects `/` to `/status` with `302`, serves `/assets/*` from `dist` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and answers every other path with `404`. The shell follows `web/DESIGN.md`, which takes the visual language of the Linear app (not of its site): a sidebar with the pages and a Repositories tree of every repository in the collection, owners expandable to their repositories, private ones marked with a lock, each linking to the inbox filtered by it, dark and light themes with dark as the default, the Inter typeface embedded in the build, a monospace stack for paths, and the brand of maintainer in the logo only; the API client with TypeScript types of every response and JSON fixtures that match the Go types, the shared components `TaskFilters` (the filter bar) and `TaskDetails` (the reading pane with the triage buttons), a table, chips, a drawer, loading and error states, the three page entry stubs with their routes, and `vitest` with `@testing-library/preact` as the test runner. `make web-check` runs `npm ci`, the TypeScript check, `npm test`, builds into a temporary directory and fails when the output differs from `web/dist` in the working tree; CI also requires every file under `web/dist` to be tracked.
- **Configuration.** `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/maintainer/service.toml`, else `~/.config/maintainer/service.toml`; a missing file means defaults, an explicitly named missing file is an error. The loader is strict like `fetch.toml`: unknown keys are errors, `internal/config/service.cue` is the schema and `make config-vet` checks valid and invalid fixtures. Keys: `[fetch] config` (path of the fetch config; default: the usual lookup with the home directory as the working directory), `[score]` with `impact`, `effort`, `type`, `age`, `due` (default 1, finite, non-negative), `age_horizon_days` (365) and `due_horizon_days` (30), both positive, and `[[repos]]` with `match` (`id`, or `owner` and `name` together, as in `fetch.toml`) and `weight` (default 1, non-negative); the first match by `id` wins, else the first by owner and name, case-insensitively. Every relative path of the service, the fetch config and the state resolves against the home directory wherever the service was launched: `brew services` runs it there. State is read through `Store.Load`; a configuration change needs a restart.
- **Index.** On start the service discovers the mirror roots through the workspace boundaries of `status` without inspecting Git: `Collect` is split into `Discover` (paths, pins, diagnostics) and the inspection; a mirror root is a real checkout row without an error, so placeholder rows (obstructions, unresolved pins), orphan rows (duplicate pin, out of scope, remote gone) and historical paths are no mirror roots and grant no write authority. It reads `.github/issues/*.md` and `.github/roadmap/*.md` of each root in the background and publishes an immutable snapshot; the pages show an "indexing" state until the first one. Three frontmatter generations parse: `issue-N.md` with an empty `code` and `[[milestone-N]]` links; `CODE-N.md` with `[[CODE-MN]]`, `issueType`, `issueFields`, `parent`, `duplicateOf` and `number: null` for a local-only issue; and the dotfiles shape, where `id` is the GitHub number, `status` and `state_reason` are lowercase and the dates are `created_at` and `updated_at`. State and reason are normalized to lowercase, dates to UTC or `null`. Comments are the trailing `<!-- <ts> <url> … -->` blocks outside fenced code; other HTML comments stay in the body. Snapshots are published under one mutex that label writes also hold: a write updates the file, reparses it and publishes a new generation; a scan remembers the generation it started from and publishes only when it is still current, otherwise it rereads the changed files and retries, so an older parse never overwrites a write. There is no automatic polling: the initial index, `POST /api/v0/refresh` and the reparse after a write. A malformed file is reported in `warnings` and keeps its previous entry, flagged `stale`.
- **Model.** A `Task` has a source key `github:<owner>/<repo>#<number>`, or `github:<owner>/<repo>:<code>` without a number; its HTTP `id` is the unpadded base64url encoding of the key, opaque to clients; its file path is provenance and never comes from the browser. It carries repository, code, title, `state` (`open|closed`), `state_reason` (`completed|not_planned|duplicate|null`), type, labels, assignees, milestone (key `github:<owner>/<repo>/milestones/<N>` and title), `issueFields`, timestamps, board memberships (board key and section as written), the derived column, flags (`ambiguous`, `contradiction`, `duplicate_mirror`, `stale`), the score with its components, and a version `"sha256-…"` of the file. Wiki links and `owner/repo#N` references resolve in the repository of the mirror they were read from; boards merge by native id (the frontmatter `id`, else `<owner>/<repo>:<file code>`) and memberships by task key, so partial copies of an organization board complete each other. The type is a non-null, non-empty `issueType`, case-insensitively, else the single `type: x` or `type:x` label, else `null`. The column is total: `closed` → `done`, or `wont_do` for `not_planned` and `duplicate`, the state always wins; `open` → by the normalized sections of its boards, To do or Todo → `todo`, In progress → `in_progress`, Backlog → `backlog`, any other section keeps its membership and yields `backlog`; boards that disagree yield `backlog` and `ambiguous`; an open task under Done or Won't do gets `contradiction` without changing the column. Column tokens: `backlog|todo|in_progress|done|wont_do`. Checkouts stay `status.Row`.
- **Score.** `score = repo_weight × (impact·w_impact + ease·w_effort + type·w_type + age·w_age + due·w_due)` with inputs clamped to `[0, 1]`: impact high 1, medium 0.5, low 0.25; ease easy 1, medium 0.5, hard 0.25; type bug 1, feature 0.5, else 0; age is the days from `created_at` to one UTC time per snapshot over `age_horizon_days`; due is 0 until `due_horizon_days` before the milestone's `due_on`, rising linearly to 1 at the due date and staying 1 after. A missing input is 0. Every order is deterministic: `updated` and `created` put a missing date last; ties break by `updated_at` descending with a missing date last, then by key ascending. Importance is a separate order: impact high, medium, low, unset, then the same ties. Components are returned.
- **Status adapter.** The package `status` exports what the TUI and HTTP share: the query over rows with sort keys and a fuzzy term (today's `queryRows`), the display cells, a structured summary and the checkout count that excludes placeholders; the TUI and `Plain` use the exported functions. The HTTP snapshot of `Collect` is cached, collected on the first request and on `POST /api/v0/checkouts/refresh`, with bounded concurrency and coalesced requests; filtering never collects.
- **API** under `/api/v0`, JSON, `Cache-Control: no-store`; every answer is the envelope `{generation, collected_at, refreshing, warnings, data}`, dates are `null` when unknown, arrays are never `null`, an error is `{error: {code, message}}` with `400` for a malformed query:
  - `GET /checkouts?q=&sort=` — the cached rows through the adapter (`sort` is a comma list of columns, `-` for descending, an unknown column is `400`); `202` with `refreshing: true` before the first snapshot; `POST /checkouts/refresh` → `202`.
  - `GET /tasks?owner=&repo=&state=&milestone=&label=&type=&assignee=&column=&q=&sort=&limit=&offset=` — `total`, `facets` (owners, repositories, milestones, labels, types, assignees, columns, states with counts over the selection, ignoring `column`, `limit` and `offset`) and a page of tasks without bodies; a repeated parameter is OR within its dimension, dimensions are AND, `label` is "all selected"; `state` is `open` by default, `closed` or `all`; `milestone` is a milestone key; `q` is a case-insensitive substring over code, title, repository and labels; `sort` is `score`, `importance`, `updated` or `created`, descending; `limit` defaults to 100, at most 500.
  - `GET /tasks/{id}` — the task with `body_html`, `comments[{at, url, html}]` rendered by goldmark (raw HTML off, URL schemes `http`, `https`, `mailto`, cached by version), its provenance, and an `ETag` equal to the version.
  - `PATCH /tasks/{id}/triage`, `application/json` only, `{"impact"?: "high"|"medium"|"low"|null, "effort"?: "easy"|"medium"|"hard"|null}`: an omitted field is unchanged, `null` removes the label, a value replaces it, an unknown or duplicate key is `400`; `If-Match` with the quoted strong ETag is required: `428` without it, `412` when the file changed, `409` for a task with duplicate mirrors, `422` for a frontmatter the patch cannot edit in place; answers the updated detail and the new `ETag`.
  - `GET /catalog` — repositories with weights, milestones, boards, labels, columns.
  - `POST /refresh` — full reconciliation, `202`.
- **Writes.** The label patch parses and validates the frontmatter but never reserializes it: only the `impact: *` and `effort: *` entries of `labels` change, in the block list, the `labels: []` form or a single-line flow list of plain scalars; several such labels, a multi-line flow list or non-scalar items are `422`; other labels, unknown fields, order, line endings (LF and CRLF), the body and the comment blocks stay byte for byte. The target is a regular file under a mirror root with no symlink in its path. The write goes to an exclusively created temporary file next to the target with the same permissions, `fsync`, a recheck of the original's hash, `rename`, `fsync` of the directory; writes are serialized by one lock. Operating limit, documented: do not run the mirror's export or push, or another editor, while triaging; the hash check plus rename does not protect against a writer between them.
- **Security.** Listeners stay literal loopback addresses. A request whose `Host` is not `maintainer.localhost`, `localhost` or an actually bound loopback literal (`127.0.0.2` is allowed by `--listen`) with that listener's port gets `421`; forwarded headers are ignored. Every mutation, both refreshes included, needs `Origin` equal to `http://<validated Host>` (missing or `null` is `403`) and the header `X-Requested-With: maintainer`; no CORS. Responses carry `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; request bodies are limited to 64 KiB.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./internal/service/hub/... ./internal/service/web/...`, `make config-vet` and `make go-dist-check` pass with Node absent from `PATH`; `make web-check` passes with Node 24.
- [ ] `httptest` covers: the three page paths, the redirect, the asset cache headers, `404` elsewhere, `421` on a foreign `Host` and `200` on a bound literal, `403` on a foreign or missing `Origin` and on a missing `X-Requested-With`, `405` and `Allow` on wrong methods, `415` on a non-JSON patch, the CSP and the other headers, and both id forms through the real router.
- [ ] A fixture mirror with the three generations, a local-only issue, an organization board with cross-repository references and partial copies in two mirrors, a disagreeing pair of boards, an open task under Done, an "Items" board, milestones with and without `dueOn`, a task without dates, a malformed file, LF and CRLF, `labels: []`, block and flow lists, hostile Markdown (raw HTML, `javascript:` links, remote images, a delimiter inside fenced code) and a duplicate mirror produces the documented tasks, columns, flags, comments and warnings; a generated mirror of 3000 tasks answers a filtered `GET /tasks` in under 100 ms warm.
- [ ] The triage patch keeps every other byte of the file (golden tests over the three generations, LF and CRLF, `labels: []`), implements omitted versus `null`, returns `400`, `409`, `412`, `422` and `428` as specified, survives a crash between the temporary file and the rename without a corrupt original, and a scan racing a write cannot publish the older parse.
- [ ] `service.toml` fixtures under `internal/config/testdata/service/{valid,invalid}/` pass `make config-vet`; the loader rejects an unknown key, a negative weight, a zero horizon, an owner-only `match` and an explicitly named missing file.
- [ ] The exported status adapter gives the TUI, `Plain` and `GET /checkouts` the same order, cells and summary for the same keys and query (table-driven test).
- [ ] Go and TypeScript DTOs agree: the JSON fixtures under `web/src/api/` decode with the Go types in a test.
- [ ] The shell renders on the owner's collection: the sidebar, both themes, indexing state, `TaskFilters` with facets, and one end-to-end flow of a filtered task list and an `impact` edit in `TaskDetails` with a `412` conflict.

## Notes from the implementation

- The API spells the custom fields `issue_fields`, snake_case like every other key; the frontmatter key stays `issueFields`.
- The dotfiles boards take their native id from `node_id`, since their `id` is a number; a board without either falls back to `<owner>/<repo>:<code>`.
- A milestone wiki link without a file resolves to the key `github:<owner>/<repo>/milestones/<link text>` with the link text as the title.
- Before the first index snapshot, `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}` and `GET /catalog` answer `202` with `data: null`, as `GET /checkouts` does; a `PATCH` before the index is `503`.
- `issueType` is lowercased, so `Feature` and the label `type: feature` meet in one facet value.
- A mirror root whose checkout has no state record takes its owner and name from `remote "origin"` in `.git/config`, read as a file.
- Known limits left for the v0.3 line: a checkout without a state record learns its identity after the discovery applied the ignore and duplicate-pin rules, so an owner/name ignore or a pinned replacement does not exclude it from the hub; owner and repository casing is part of the identity key, so two mirrors of one repository that differ only in case are not merged.
- The sidebar has **Reindex**, which posts `/api/v0/refresh` and reloads the page once the generation changed; a `412` on a triage reparses the file first, so the page's reload gets the current ETag.
- The writer edits a non-empty single-line flow list `labels: ["a", "b"]` in place as well, keeping the neighbours' quoting style: the dotfiles mirror uses that form; a multi-line flow list or non-scalar items stay `422`.

## Out of scope

The three pages' presentation; GitHub synchronization; automatic polling or a file watcher; an advisory lock shared with the mirror tooling; a session cookie; browser end-to-end tests; drag and drop; a Linux service.
